question.text: Two separate wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are stretched by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> respectively, when they are subjected to a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Assume that both the wires are made up of same material and the radius of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> times that of the radius of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The length of the wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> can be expressed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____.
